Q: vbscript to delete rows in an excel sheet using a specific condition A:

This task can be solved with Excel formula too.

The formula to apply on the data range is: (See Example1)

=LET(table,A3:E18,
colA,TAKE(table,,1),
filt,BYROW(colA,LAMBDA(x,IF(AND(x<>"",OFFSET(x,2,0)<>""),ROW(x),-1))),
filt2,IF(TAKE(colA,-2)<>"",MAX(ROW(table)-1),-1),
disprow,SORT(VSTACK(filt,filt+1,filt2,filt2+1),1),
CHOOSEROWS(table,FILTER(disprow,disprow>0)-ROW(TAKE(table,1))+1))

There is only one parameter to define, which is the range to process.
This is set in the first row to the table variable.
The formula can return the last row too if it contains a code value. (See Example2)

To display empty(zero length string) value instead of 0 in the result replace the last row in the formula with:

res,CHOOSEROWS(table,FILTER(disprow,disprow>0)-ROW(TAKE(table,1))+1),
IF(res=0,"",res))

This workaround works if there is no real 0 value in the other columns of the table.

Other workarounds can be found Display or hide zero values

Q: Failed SSL handshake in Kafka Producer A:

Apparently not the issue here but I have been struggling with the same error for a while and in my case the kafka-console-producer.sh was failing with the similar errors:

$ kafka-console-producer.sh --broker-list 192.168.1.173:9093 --topic kafka-security-topic --producer.config ~/ssl/client-ssl-auth.properties
org.apache.kafka.common.errors.SslAuthenticationException: SSL handshake failed
Caused by: javax.net.ssl.SSLHandshakeException: General SSLEngine problem

checking with debug

$ export KAFKA_OPTS="-Djavax.net.debug=ssl"

kafka-producer-network-thread | console-producer, fatal error: 46: General SSLEngine problem
java.security.cert.CertificateException: No subject alternative names present
%% Invalidated:  [Session-1, TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA384]
kafka-producer-network-thread | console-producer, SEND TLSv1.2 ALERT:  fatal, description = certificate_unknown
[2021-07-13 16:21:53,909] ERROR [Producer clientId=console-producer] Connection to node -1 (/192.168.1.173:9093) failed authentication due to: SSL handshake failed (org.apache.kafka.clients.NetworkClient)

In my case turned out the reason is using IP instead of hostname when specifying broker-list parameter.

That worked:

$ kafka-console-producer.sh --broker-list red03:9093 --topic kafka-security-topic --producer.config ~/ssl/client-ssl-auth.properties

Q: How to set the .env file to link laravel to Mysql? A:

If you're using Homestead, you should use these settings:

DB_CONNECTION=mysql
DB_HOST=127.0.0.1
DB_PORT=3306
DB_DATABASE=db_name
DB_USERNAME=homestead
DB_PASSWORD=secret

Also, you should connect to MySQL and create db_name database to use it.

Q: Embedding Visio Files in SharePoint A:

The page jumps to the beginning of the embedding frame behavior is browser focus-scroll on the iframe, not a Visio hyperlink setting.

&wdClickOnlyHyperlinks=true is the right parameter for the first part: Microsoft documents that embedded Visio links use Ctrl+Click by default, and that adding &wdClickOnlyHyperlinks=true to the iframe src changes them to click-only links.

The second behavior happens before Visio handles the shape click. On the first click, the embedded Office/Visio iframe receives focus, and the browser scrolls that focused frame into view (scrollIntoView-style behavior). That click is then effectively used to focus the frame; after the frame is focused, later clicks reach the Visio content normally.

There is no documented Visio/Office embed URL parameter that disables that first focus-scroll. Without JavaScript, the practical mitigations are layout ones:

  • put the Embed Web Part at or near the top of the SharePoint page, so scrolling the iframe into view causes little or no visible jump;
  • fit the Visio diagram/zoom so the useful content starts at the top of the embedded frame;
  • test the SharePoint File and media web part instead of the raw Embed Web Part.

If the embed must remain lower on the page and the jump must be eliminated completely, that crosses into intercepting focus behavior, which requires JavaScript.

Q: What must a type satisfy for its auto-generated hash function to be copy-constructible? A:

The latest C++ draft: 16.4.4.5 Cpp17Hash requirements [hash.requirements]

  1. A type H meets the Cpp17Hash requirements if

    1. — it is a function object type,
    2. — it meets the Cpp17CopyConstructible and Cpp17Destructible requirements, and
    3. — the expressions shown in Table 37 are valid and have the indicated semantics

  2. Given Key is an argument type for function objects of type H, in Table 37 h is a value of type (possibly const) H, u is an lvalue of type Key, and k is a value of a type convertible to (possibly const) Key.

Table 37 — Cpp17Hash requirements [tab:cpp17.hash]

Expression Return type Requirement
h(k) size_t The value returned shall depend only on the argument k for the duration of the program.
[Note 1 : Thus all evaluations of the expression h(k) with the same value for k yield the same result for a given execution of the program. — end note]
For two different values t1 and t2, the probability that h(t1) and h(t2) compare equal should be very small, approaching 1.0 / numeric_limits<size_t>::max().
h(u) size_t Shall not modify u.

Note that the unordered associative container requirements (23.2.8.1, 29, 32, 41, 44, 53, and 56) impose Cpp17DefaultConstructible as a precondition on hasher for any constructor that doesn't take an explicit hf (hasher function) argument. Specifically:

  • X(n) — Preconditions: hasher and key_equal meet the Cpp17DefaultConstructible requirements.
  • X a = X() / X a — same precondition.
  • X(i, j, n) — same.
  • X(i, j) — same.
  • X(from_range, rg, n) — same.
  • X(from_range, rg) — same.
  • X(il) — equivalent to X(il.begin(), il.end()), which has the same precondition.

what requirements must a type satisfy, to ensure its default hash function std::hash<_Tp> is default-constructible?

Having a default constructor is a good start. To also make it copy constructible, it needs a copy constructor.

For hash functions in general, having state is usually questionable since the value returned by the hash function shall only depend on the argument. Making it stateless and leaving all constructors and the destructor automatically generated by the implementation is usually the way to do it.
